title: Objects
goal: This lesson covers how to make objects from a class by calling the class name with parentheses.
idea: An object is one real thing built from the class blueprint. You make one by calling the class name like a function, like dog1 = Dog(). You can make as many objects from the same class as you like, and each one is a separate thing.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, create dog3 = Dog() and print a message about it, then press Run.

practice.text: Make two Pet objects and print a message that you made two pets.
practice.hint: Finish a = and b = with Pet(). Call the class like a function. Then print() a sentence saying you made two pets.
practice.starterTip: a = Pet() and b = Pet(), then print("Made two pets") or similar.
practice.starter:
class Pet:
    pass
a = 
b = 
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if two Pet() objects are created and a message prints.

practice.text: Create three Coin objects. Print how many you made (3).
practice.hint: Use three variables with any names you like and assign Coin() to each. Your print should show the number 3.
practice.starterTip: c1 = Coin(), c2 = Coin(), c3 = Coin(), then print("Made", 3) or print(3).
practice.gradingNote: Pass if three Coin() creations and print shows 3.

quiz.question: How do you make an object from Dog?
quiz.correct: Right, you call the class name with parentheses.

quiz.question: Are dog1 and dog2 the same object?

options.text: They share one memory forever forced

quiz.correct: Yes, every call makes a new object.
quiz.wrong: It is two builds from one blueprint.

quiz.question: What do you store Dog() in?
quiz.correct: Right, a variable holds the object.
